title: Kune Food's Last Day, With 55,000 Meals Sold and No Next Round
conflicts: Closure year: slate said 2023, all sources say 22 June 2022; 2022 used. Operating span: about a year (TechCrunch, The Star) vs ten months (Citizen Digital, Kenyans.co.ke headlines) vs four or six months (TechMoran, The Standard); story gives founding and funding dates instead of a span. Pre-seed in shillings: Ksh100m, Ksh107m, Ksh112m; story uses $1 million. TechMoran says Kune 'raised' $3.5m while TechCrunch, Citizen Digital and Reecht say the round failed; Reecht's account used. Staff: about 90 vs over 90 vs nearly 100; 'about ninety' used. The Star's report that an investor withdrew rests on unnamed reports and is omitted; The Citizen (Tanzania) column's margin figures and critique are not used.
notes: Blame is limited to Reecht's own LinkedIn statement (downturn, investment markets, food costs, $3 meals, 'many things could have been done differently'). The 2021 launch controversy is mentioned factually with Kune's apology. Quote stance: complicates (Saadi's merchant who hides his loss, set against Reecht's public closure).
